summary: Backend chunked invoice upload + decoupled extraction VERIFIED end-to-end. 6/6 pytest cases pass against the production-style external URL: single-chunk happy path (job → done with equipment_count=1, page_count=1, supplier_name, import_id present), multi-chunk reassembly with a ~3.2MB real PDF (>=2 chunks, reassembled, extraction returned equipment_count>=1), finalize with bogus upload_id → 404 'Upload not found or expired' (no 520/hang), corrupt non-PDF bytes surface a clean job-level error (status=error with message), chunk docs are deleted immediately after finalize (re-finalize same upload_id → 404), and finalize returns immediately (<10s, status=processing — no synchronous long-hold). Frontend UI could NOT be driven because the master-admin SPA fails to bootstrap under the test harness's CSP (the SPA's main script bundle from assets.emergent.sh + posthog + cloudflareinsights are CSP-blocked, so post-login the app stays on /login). This matches the explicit note in the review request to fall back to backend verification in that case.

integration_issues.flow: Master-admin onboarding wizard via testing harness
integration_issues.issue: Post-login the SPA does not advance — 3rd-party scripts (assets.emergent.sh/scripts/emergent-main.js, posthog, cloudflareinsights beacon) are blocked by CSP in this preview env, so the master-admin shell never finishes booting and /master-admin/onboarding falls through to the public 404. Not a regression from this fix — same behaviour as prior iterations. Backend chunked flow is fully proven via pytest.

critical_code_review_comments: routes/equipment_import.py: chunks are stored in MongoDB (db.invoice_upload_chunks) — works across replicas ✅. Stale chunks for the same upload_id are wiped on chunk_index==0 (good — prevents cross-upload contamination if a client retries with the same id).

/parse-invoice/finalize runs validate_upload synchronously then asyncio.create_task(_worker()) — correct pattern: client-facing 4xx for obviously bad files, background job for slow LLM extraction. job_id is returned immediately (verified ≤10s).
Worker writes status=error with the exception message — clean error surfacing, no hung 520s.
Minor (not blocking): _CHUNK_DIR='/tmp/pulse_invoice_chunks' constant at line 635 is now dead code (chunks live in Mongo). Safe to delete to avoid future confusion.

Minor: db.invoice_upload_chunks has no documented TTL index — if a client uploads chunks and never calls finalize, those documents persist. Consider adding a TTL on `created_at` (e.g. 1h) so abandoned uploads self-clean.

success_rate.frontend: not testable in this harness (CSP blocks master-admin SPA bootstrap)

No fixture-side teardown was added because each test uses fresh random upload_ids and the chunked docs are wiped by finalize.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run from /app/backend: `python -m pytest tests/test_chunked_invoice_upload_jan2026.py -v`. Test file uses REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL (falls back to reading /app/frontend/.env). Multi-chunk PDF is built by inserting a noisy JPEG per page until size >= 3.2MB (PyMuPDF/fitz). Multi-chunk extraction can take ~30-60s — _poll timeout is 240s. Frontend UI tests for the onboarding dropzone require the master-admin SPA to actually boot; under the preview CSP it does not (scripts from assets.emergent.sh are blocked). E1 may want to either (a) self-test the dropzone manually in a real browser, or (b) relax CSP for the preview environment so future automated UI runs can drive /master-admin/onboarding. Backend chunked flow itself is rock-solid and matches the fix described in the review request.
rca of the issue: Original prod 520: small invoices (<=1.5MB) hit /api/equipment-import/parse-invoice synchronously and the AI extraction inside the request frequently exceeded Cloudflare's ~100s gateway timeout. Fix verified here: every invoice now goes through chunk → finalize → background job → poll. Finalize returns <1s with a job_id (no long-hold request to hit the gateway timeout); extraction happens in asyncio.create_task so a client disconnect cannot cancel it; chunks live in MongoDB so any replica can finalize regardless of which replica received the chunks.
